paper.title_en: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
paper.abstract_en: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.
